report.verdict: alive (after the one rule change: life 30)
report.numbers: Life 30: Expert beats Random 100%, Greedy 90.0%, Racer 88.5% (400 games each, seats alternated); Expert equals Greedy in 47.0% of 40,274 decisions (32.5% of pitch decisions); first player wins 67.5% of 400 Expert mirror games; 0 games hit the turn cap; Expert passes all three set positions on 5 seeds each. As specified (life 20) it failed only the first-player line: 73.8% over 600 Expert mirror games (70.5% of the gate's 200, 75.5% of 400 more), with Expert at 100/88.8/83.8% against Random/Greedy/Racer.
loop: Each turn a player turns the whole hand into one or two plays: Expert pitches 3.6 cards and plays 1.7 a turn, and empties its hand in 86.5% of turns.

Because a pitched card goes under the deck and the hand refills to five, pitching is free cycling: a third of Expert's pitches (33%) buy mana it never spends, to swap a card it does not want (Big, Hit 5: pitch 1) for a fresh draw. Holding cards for next turn almost never happens (0.15 left in hand a turn).

So the real decision is which one or two cards to play and which to burn: Pips (pitch 3) are money far more often than bodies; Hits go at units to win the board and at the player to finish. Expert disagrees with Greedy's pitch-the-highest rule on two pitch decisions in three.
Still a race at heart: the first player wins 67.5% of Expert mirrors even at 30 life, close to the line.
report.cost: Paying binds every turn in the sense that a hand of five buys one or two plays, but mana itself rarely limits: the pool is left over in 52.7% of turns (1.58 a turn), because surplus pitches are taken for cycling, not for mana. A card that could not be paid for even pitching everything else is in hand in 12.8% of turns.

ruleChange.why: At 20 life the Expert mirror lasted 7.9 turns (four each) and the first player won 73.8% of 600 Expert mirror games: in a four-turn race the first player's extra attack turn is a quarter of the game, and starting one card short (4 against 5) does not pay for it. 30 life lengthens the race by half so a single tempo step weighs less, without touching the pitch economy the concept tests.
